newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares ease in quiet trade; UES seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares ease in quiet trade; UES seen up.

text.p: Early trade was thin in leading Russian shares, and traders said they saw the market quiet with fluctuations on short-term speculation in national power utility UES and position-taking ahead of Thursday's national holiday.
President Boris Yeltsin signed decrees on natural monopoly regulation and on telecoms but traders said it was hard to predict what the effect on the market would be until details were available.
"We'll see what happens. There's been lots of talking over last two weeks and it's not had a great effect yet," said senior Trinfiko trader Grigory Pensky.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 shares opened at 297.76 after closing at 297.60 on Friday.
But national power company UES slipped to $0.2247 at GMT 0925 after closing on Friday at $0.2262 and regional utility Mosenergo fell to $1.245 from $1.257.
Traders said they were optimistic that growth could still follow what they said was just a technical correction.
"Indications from the morning say it's possible that foreign investors will continue to buy UES," said Oleg Martynenko, head of equity sales and trading at Rossiisky Kredit Bank.
He said he expected Mosenergo to follow UES up, although he saw short-term speculation causing the UES price to fluctuate.

"There were lots of foreign and Russian investors on Friday as well as lot of speculators interested in short term playing," Martynenko said. "They will take profits today and tomorrow, trying to make the market fluctuate."
But traders, despite expecting isolated big orders ahead of the market holidays this week and next, saw prices remaining range-bound in the short-term.
"Operators are building up their positions for the long holidays," said Martynenko. "The market will generally be quiet but it might sometimes be driven up and down on certain shares."
